meta.topic: 多元微积分：曲面积分、散度与旋度、隐函数求导、多元泰勒

zh: 设曲面 $\Sigma$ 有正则参数表示 $\boldsymbol r(u,v)$，$(u,v)\in D$，且 $\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v\ne\boldsymbol 0$，$f$ 在 $\Sigma$ 上连续。把 $D$ 分成小格，第 $i$ 格对应曲面小块 $\Delta S_i$，记 $\lambda$ 为所有小格直径的最大值；当 $\lambda\to0$ 时，小块近似为平行四边形，两边向量为 $\boldsymbol r_u\Delta u$、$\boldsymbol r_v\Delta v$，故 $\Delta S_i\approx|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|\,\Delta u\,\Delta v$。当 $f$ 连续、$\Sigma$ 光滑时，下述和式的极限存在且与分法、取点无关，于是第一类曲面积分定义为 $\iint_\Sigma f\,dS=\lim\limits_{\lambda\to0}\sum_i f(\boldsymbol r(u_i,v_i))|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|\,\Delta u_i\,\Delta v_i$，即面积元素 $dS=|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|\,du\,dv$。这里只累加面积，未指定法向，所以积分与曲面的侧无关。

特例：若 $\Sigma$ 是图 $z=z(x,y)$，$(x,y)\in D_{xy}$，且 $z$ 有连续偏导，取 $\boldsymbol r(x,y)=(x,y,z(x,y))$。则 $\boldsymbol r_x=(1,0,z_x)$，$\boldsymbol r_y=(0,1,z_y)$，$\boldsymbol r_x\times\boldsymbol r_y=(-z_x,-z_y,1)$，故 $|\boldsymbol r_x\times\boldsymbol r_y|=\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}$。于是 $dS=\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}\,dx\,dy$，且 $$\iint_\Sigma f\,dS=\iint_{D_{xy}}f\big(x,y,z(x,y)\big)\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}\,dx\,dy.$$ 这里要求 $\Sigma$ 能整体写成该图（否则分片处理），$f$ 连续以保证可积。

定向：正则曲面上每点有两个单位法向 $\pm\boldsymbol n$，其中 $\boldsymbol n=\dfrac{\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v}{|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|}$；交换 $u,v$（或作定向相反的重参数化）会翻转 $\boldsymbol n$。第二类曲面积分必须先选定一侧。以 $\iint_\Sigma R\,dx\,dy$ 为例，其定义为 $\lim\limits_{\lambda\to0}\sum_i R(\xi_i,\eta_i,\zeta_i)(\Delta S_i)_{xy}$，其中 $(\Delta S_i)_{xy}$ 是小块在 $xy$ 平面上的带符号投影面积。若 $\boldsymbol n=(\cos\alpha,\cos\beta,\cos\gamma)$，则 $(\Delta S_i)_{xy}\approx\cos\gamma\,\Delta S_i$，故 $\iint_\Sigma R\,dx\,dy=\iint_\Sigma R\cos\gamma\,dS$。

同理，$dy\,dz$ 对应 $yz$ 平面的带符号投影，符号因子为 $\cos\alpha$；$dz\,dx$ 对应 $zx$ 平面，符号因子为 $\cos\beta$。三式相加得两类曲面积分的关系 $$\begin{aligned}\iint_\Sigma &P\,dy\,dz+Q\,dz\,dx+R\,dx\,dy\\ &=\iint_\Sigma(P\cos\alpha+Q\cos\beta+R\cos\gamma)\,dS\\ &=\iint_\Sigma\boldsymbol F\cdot\boldsymbol n\,dS,\end{aligned}$$ 其中 $\boldsymbol F=(P,Q,R)$。右端正是流速场 $\boldsymbol F$ 穿过定向曲面 $\Sigma$ 的通量；把 $\boldsymbol n$ 换成 $-\boldsymbol n$ 时右端整体变号，所以第二类积分换侧变号，而第一类积分不变。

图情形取上侧：$\boldsymbol n=\dfrac{(-z_x,-z_y,1)}{\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}}$，故 $\cos\gamma=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}}$，且 $\boldsymbol F\cdot\boldsymbol n\,dS=(-Pz_x-Qz_y+R)\,dx\,dy$。于是 $$\begin{aligned}&\iint_\Sigma P\,dy\,dz+Q\,dz\,dx+R\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad=\iint_{D_{xy}}(-Pz_x-Qz_y+R)\,dx\,dy\quad(\text{取上侧});\end{aligned}$$ 其中 $P,Q,R$ 均在 $(x,y,z(x,y))$ 处取值。取下侧时 $\boldsymbol n$ 反向，整体加负号。若曲面不能整体写成图，就分成若干片分别投影后相加，并要求各片定向相容。

例：上半球面 $\Sigma:z=\sqrt{a^2-x^2-y^2}$，$D_{xy}:x^2+y^2\le a^2$。此时 $z_x=-x/z$，$z_y=-y/z$，$\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}=a/z$，故 $$\iint_\Sigma z\,dS=\iint_{D_{xy}}z\cdot\frac{a}{z}\,dx\,dy=a\cdot\pi a^2=\pi a^3.$$ 再取上侧算第二类：$$\begin{aligned}\iint_\Sigma z\,dx\,dy&=\iint_{D_{xy}}\sqrt{a^2-x^2-y^2}\,dx\,dy\\ &=2\pi\int_0^a r\sqrt{a^2-r^2}\,dr=\frac{2\pi a^3}{3};\end{aligned}$$ 若取下侧，则结果为 $-\dfrac{2\pi a^3}{3}$，定向符号由此得到验证。
en: Let $\Sigma$ have a regular parametrization $\boldsymbol r(u,v)$, $(u,v)\in D$, with $\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v\ne\boldsymbol 0$, and let $f$ be continuous on $\Sigma$. Subdivide $D$ into small cells; the $i$-th cell corresponds to a surface patch of area $\Delta S_i$. Let $\lambda$ be the largest diameter of the cells. As $\lambda\to0$, the patch is approximately the parallelogram spanned by $\boldsymbol r_u\Delta u$ and $\boldsymbol r_v\Delta v$, so $\Delta S_i\approx|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|\,\Delta u\,\Delta v$. When $f$ is continuous and $\Sigma$ is smooth, the limit of these sums exists and is independent of the subdivision and sample points, so the first-kind surface integral is defined by $\iint_\Sigma f\,dS=\lim\limits_{\lambda\to0}\sum_i f(\boldsymbol r(u_i,v_i))|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|\,\Delta u_i\,\Delta v_i$, that is, $dS=|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|\,du\,dv$. Only area is accumulated and no normal is chosen, so the integral does not depend on the side of the surface.

Special case: if $\Sigma$ is the graph $z=z(x,y)$ over $(x,y)\in D_{xy}$ with continuous partials, take $\boldsymbol r(x,y)=(x,y,z(x,y))$. Then $\boldsymbol r_x=(1,0,z_x)$, $\boldsymbol r_y=(0,1,z_y)$ and $\boldsymbol r_x\times\boldsymbol r_y=(-z_x,-z_y,1)$, so $|\boldsymbol r_x\times\boldsymbol r_y|=\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}$. Thus $dS=\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}\,dx\,dy$ and $$\iint_\Sigma f\,dS=\iint_{D_{xy}}f\big(x,y,z(x,y)\big)\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}\,dx\,dy.$$ Here $\Sigma$ must be a single graph (otherwise split it into pieces), and continuity of $f$ ensures integrability.

Orientation: at each point of a regular surface there are two unit normals $\pm\boldsymbol n$, where $\boldsymbol n=\dfrac{\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v}{|\boldsymbol r_u\times\boldsymbol r_v|}$; swapping $u,v$ (or reversing the orientation of the parametrization) reverses $\boldsymbol n$. A second-kind integral requires a chosen side. For $\iint_\Sigma R\,dx\,dy$, the definition is $\lim\limits_{\lambda\to0}\sum_i R(\xi_i,\eta_i,\zeta_i)(\Delta S_i)_{xy}$, where $(\Delta S_i)_{xy}$ is the signed area of the projection of the patch onto the $xy$-plane. If $\boldsymbol n=(\cos\alpha,\cos\beta,\cos\gamma)$, then $(\Delta S_i)_{xy}\approx\cos\gamma\,\Delta S_i$, hence $\iint_\Sigma R\,dx\,dy=\iint_\Sigma R\cos\gamma\,dS$.

Similarly, $dy\,dz$ uses the signed projection onto the $yz$-plane with factor $\cos\alpha$, and $dz\,dx$ uses the $zx$-plane with factor $\cos\beta$. Adding the three identities gives the relation between the two kinds: $$\begin{aligned}\iint_\Sigma &P\,dy\,dz+Q\,dz\,dx+R\,dx\,dy\\ &=\iint_\Sigma(P\cos\alpha+Q\cos\beta+R\cos\gamma)\,dS\\ &=\iint_\Sigma\boldsymbol F\cdot\boldsymbol n\,dS,\end{aligned}$$ with $\boldsymbol F=(P,Q,R)$. The right-hand side is the flux of the velocity field $\boldsymbol F$ through the oriented surface $\Sigma$; replacing $\boldsymbol n$ by $-\boldsymbol n$ flips the sign, so a second-kind integral changes sign with the side while a first-kind integral does not.

For a graph taken on the upper side, $\boldsymbol n=\dfrac{(-z_x,-z_y,1)}{\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}}$, so $\cos\gamma=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}}$ and $\boldsymbol F\cdot\boldsymbol n\,dS=(-Pz_x-Qz_y+R)\,dx\,dy$. Therefore $$\begin{aligned}&\iint_\Sigma P\,dy\,dz+Q\,dz\,dx+R\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad=\iint_{D_{xy}}(-Pz_x-Qz_y+R)\,dx\,dy\quad(\text{upper side});\end{aligned}$$ where $P,Q,R$ are evaluated at $(x,y,z(x,y))$. On the lower side $\boldsymbol n$ reverses and the whole integral changes sign. A surface that is not a single graph must be split into pieces, projected separately, and the orientations must be compatible.

Example: the upper hemisphere $\Sigma:z=\sqrt{a^2-x^2-y^2}$ over $D_{xy}:x^2+y^2\le a^2$. Here $z_x=-x/z$, $z_y=-y/z$ and $\sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}=a/z$, hence $$\iint_\Sigma z\,dS=\iint_{D_{xy}}z\cdot\frac{a}{z}\,dx\,dy=a\cdot\pi a^2=\pi a^3.$$ For the second kind, upper side: $$\begin{aligned}\iint_\Sigma z\,dx\,dy&=\iint_{D_{xy}}\sqrt{a^2-x^2-y^2}\,dx\,dy\\ &=2\pi\int_0^a r\sqrt{a^2-r^2}\,dr=\frac{2\pi a^3}{3};\end{aligned}$$ on the lower side the value is $-\dfrac{2\pi a^3}{3}$, confirming the orientation sign.

zh: 设 $\boldsymbol F=(P,Q,R)$ 有连续一阶偏导。散度的坐标无关定义是通量密度：取包含点 $M$ 的小区域 $\Omega$，体积 $V=|\Omega|$，边界 $\partial\Omega$ 取外法向 $\boldsymbol n$，则 $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F(M)=\lim\limits_{V\to0}\dfrac{1}{V}\iint_{\partial\Omega}\boldsymbol F\cdot\boldsymbol n\,dS$。为导出坐标公式，取以 $M=(x,y,z)$ 为一个顶点、边长 $h,k,\ell$ 的长方体。$x$ 方向一对对面的通量之差为 $[P(x+h,y,z)-P(x,y,z)]k\ell\approx P_x hk\ell$，除以 $V=hk\ell$ 得 $P_x$；$y,z$ 方向同理。

三个方向相加即得 $$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F=\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial R}{\partial z}=\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol F,$$ 它是一个标量。$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F(M)>0$ 表示 $M$ 附近净流出，像有源；$<0$ 表示净流入，像有汇；$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F\equiv0$ 的场称为无源场，不可压缩流体的速度场即满足此式。例如 $\boldsymbol F=(x,y,z)$ 有 $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F=3$，每一点都是源；$\boldsymbol F=(-y,x,0)$ 的散度为零，流体既不压缩也不膨胀。

旋度的坐标无关定义是环量密度：对过 $M$ 的单位法向 $\boldsymbol n$ 和以 $\boldsymbol n$ 为法向的小曲面片 $S$，规定边界 $\partial S$ 的定向与 $\boldsymbol n$ 成右手法则，则 $(\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F(M))\cdot\boldsymbol n=\lim\limits_{A\to0}\dfrac{1}{A}\oint_{\partial S}\boldsymbol F\cdot d\boldsymbol r$，$A=|S|$。取 $S$ 为 $xy$ 平面内以 $(x,y)$ 为左下角、边长 $h,k$ 的矩形，从 $+z$ 方向看逆时针绕行。四条边的环量之和约为 $[Q(x+h,y)-Q(x,y)]k-[P(x,y+k)-P(x,y)]h\approx(Q_x-P_y)hk$，除以 $A=hk$ 得 $z$ 分量 $\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y}$。

对 $yz$ 平面和 $zx$ 平面内的矩形作同样计算，并按 $x\to y\to z$ 循环，得 $$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F=\Big(&\frac{\partial R}{\partial y}-\frac{\partial Q}{\partial z},\ \frac{\partial P}{\partial z}-\frac{\partial R}{\partial x},\\ &\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\Big)=\nabla\times\boldsymbol F,\end{aligned}$$ 它是一个向量。物理上旋度刻画局部旋转：刚体绕 $z$ 轴以角速度 $\omega$ 转动时 $\boldsymbol F=(-\omega y,\omega x,0)$，而 $\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F=(0,0,2\omega)$，即旋度是角速度的两倍；$\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F\equiv\boldsymbol0$ 的场称为无旋场。

若 $f$ 与 $\boldsymbol F$ 有连续二阶偏导，则二阶混合偏导相等。于是 $\operatorname{rot}(\operatorname{grad}f)=\boldsymbol0$：例如第一个分量为 $\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(f_z)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(f_y)=f_{zy}-f_{yz}=0$。同理 $$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(R_y-Q_z)+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(P_z-R_x)\\ &\quad+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(Q_x-P_y)=0,\end{aligned}$$ 六项两两抵消。故梯度场必无旋、旋度场必无散；另有 $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{grad}f)=\Delta f$。

在单连通区域上且 $\boldsymbol F$ 连续可偏导时，$\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F=\boldsymbol0$ 等价于存在势函数 $u$ 使 $\boldsymbol F=\operatorname{grad}u$，也等价于沿任意闭曲线的环量为零、积分与路径无关。单连通不能省：$\boldsymbol F=\left(\dfrac{-y}{x^2+y^2},\dfrac{x}{x^2+y^2},0\right)$ 在挖去 $z$ 轴的区域内旋度处处为零，但绕 $z$ 轴一周的环量为 $2\pi$，故不存在单值势函数。
en: Let $\boldsymbol F=(P,Q,R)$ have continuous first partials. The coordinate-free definition of divergence is flux density: for a small region $\Omega$ containing $M$ with volume $V=|\Omega|$ and outward normal $\boldsymbol n$ on $\partial\Omega$, $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F(M)=\lim\limits_{V\to0}\dfrac{1}{V}\iint_{\partial\Omega}\boldsymbol F\cdot\boldsymbol n\,dS$. To obtain the coordinate formula, take a box with one vertex at $M=(x,y,z)$ and side lengths $h,k,\ell$. The net flux through the pair of faces normal to the $x$-axis is $[P(x+h,y,z)-P(x,y,z)]k\ell\approx P_x hk\ell$; dividing by $V=hk\ell$ gives $P_x$, and the $y$ and $z$ directions are identical.

Adding the three directions, $$\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F=\frac{\partial P}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial Q}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial R}{\partial z}=\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol F,$$ a scalar. $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F(M)>0$ means a net outflow near $M$, i.e. a source; $<0$ means a net inflow, i.e. a sink; fields with $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F\equiv0$ are source-free, as is the velocity field of an incompressible fluid. For $\boldsymbol F=(x,y,z)$, $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol F=3$ and every point is a source; for $\boldsymbol F=(-y,x,0)$ the divergence vanishes, so the flow neither compresses nor expands.

The coordinate-free definition of curl is circulation density: for a unit normal $\boldsymbol n$ through $M$ and a small surface patch $S$ normal to $\boldsymbol n$, orient $\partial S$ by the right-hand rule with respect to $\boldsymbol n$. Then $(\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F(M))\cdot\boldsymbol n=\lim\limits_{A\to0}\dfrac{1}{A}\oint_{\partial S}\boldsymbol F\cdot d\boldsymbol r$, $A=|S|$. Take $S$ to be the rectangle in the $xy$-plane with lower-left corner $(x,y)$ and sides $h,k$, traversed counterclockwise as seen from $+z$. The circulation around its four edges is approximately $[Q(x+h,y)-Q(x,y)]k-[P(x,y+k)-P(x,y)]h\approx(Q_x-P_y)hk$; dividing by $A=hk$ gives the $z$-component $\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y}$.

Performing the same computation for rectangles in the $yz$- and $zx$-planes and cycling $x\to y\to z$ yields $$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F=\Big(&\frac{\partial R}{\partial y}-\frac{\partial Q}{\partial z},\ \frac{\partial P}{\partial z}-\frac{\partial R}{\partial x},\\ &\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\Big)=\nabla\times\boldsymbol F,\end{aligned}$$ a vector. Physically the curl measures local rotation: a rigid body rotating about the $z$-axis with angular velocity $\omega$ has $\boldsymbol F=(-\omega y,\omega x,0)$ and $\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F=(0,0,2\omega)$, so the curl is twice the angular velocity; fields with $\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F\equiv\boldsymbol0$ are called irrotational.

If $f$ and $\boldsymbol F$ have continuous second partials, mixed partials commute. Then $\operatorname{rot}(\operatorname{grad}f)=\boldsymbol0$: for instance its first component is $\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(f_z)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(f_y)=f_{zy}-f_{yz}=0$. Likewise $$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F)&=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(R_y-Q_z)+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(P_z-R_x)\\ &\quad+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(Q_x-P_y)=0,\end{aligned}$$ since the six terms cancel in pairs. Hence gradient fields are irrotational and curl fields are source-free; also $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{grad}f)=\Delta f$.

On a simply connected region, with $\boldsymbol F$ continuously differentiable, $\operatorname{rot}\boldsymbol F=\boldsymbol0$ is equivalent to the existence of a potential $u$ with $\boldsymbol F=\operatorname{grad}u$, and also to the vanishing of the circulation around every closed curve, i.e. path independence. Simple connectivity cannot be dropped: $\boldsymbol F=\left(\dfrac{-y}{x^2+y^2},\dfrac{x}{x^2+y^2},0\right)$ has zero curl on the region with the $z$-axis removed, yet its circulation around the $z$-axis equals $2\pi$, so no single-valued potential exists.

zh: 设 $F(x,y,z)$ 在点 $P_0=(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ 的某邻域内有连续偏导，$F(P_0)=0$，且 $F_z(P_0)\ne0$。隐函数存在定理断言：存在 $(x_0,y_0)$ 的邻域 $U$ 和唯一的连续可微函数 $z=\varphi(x,y)$（其值在 $z_0$ 附近），使 $\varphi(x_0,y_0)=z_0$，且在 $U$ 上恒有 $F(x,y,\varphi(x,y))=0$；若 $F$ 还有连续的高阶偏导，则 $\varphi$ 也有相应阶的连续偏导。

条件 $F_z(P_0)
e0$ 是局部可解性的关键。把 $F$ 在 $P_0$ 处线性化：$F(x_0+\Delta x,y_0+\Delta y,z_0+\Delta z)\approx F_x\Delta x+F_y\Delta y+F_z\Delta z$。线性主部中 $\Delta z$ 的系数是 $F_z$；当 $F_z
e0$ 时可由主部唯一解出 $\Delta z\approx-\dfrac{F_x\Delta x+F_y\Delta y}{F_z}$，这正是定理假设 $F_z
e0$ 的由来。若 $F_z=0$，线性化不能确定 $\Delta z$，隐函数可能不存在、不唯一或不可微。反例：$F(x,y,z)=z^2-x^2-y^2$ 在原点满足 $F=0$ 但 $F_z=0$，方程 $z^2=x^2+y^2$ 在原点附近给出 $z=\pm\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ 两支，不能唯一确定一个过原点的可微函数 $z=\varphi(x,y)$。

在 $U$ 上把 $z=\varphi(x,y)$ 代回方程，得恒等式 $F(x,y,\varphi(x,y))\equiv0$。由于 $F_z$ 连续且 $F_z(P_0)
e0$，在 $P_0$ 的某邻域内仍有 $F_z
e0$；必要时缩小 $U$，即可在该邻域内做除法。固定 $y$ 对 $x$ 求偏导，由链式法则 $$F_x(x,y,\varphi)+F_z(x,y,\varphi)\,\varphi_x=0.$$ 因 $F_z
e0$，可解出 $\varphi_x=-\dfrac{F_x}{F_z}$；对 $y$ 同理得 $\varphi_y=-\dfrac{F_y}{F_z}$。三个偏导都在 $(x,y,\varphi(x,y))$ 处取值。公式说明：不必解出 $z$ 的显式表达式，只需计算 $F$ 的偏导。

几何解释：$F(x,y,z)=0$ 是等值面，$
abla F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$ 是它的法向量；而 $z=\varphi(x,y)$ 的图像法向量可取 $(-\varphi_x,-\varphi_y,1)$。两者平行，故 $$(-\varphi_x,-\varphi_y,1)= rac{1}{F_z}(F_x,F_y,F_z),$$ 即 $\varphi_x=-F_x/F_z$、$\varphi_y=-F_y/F_z$。若在 $
abla F(P_0)
e0$ 时仍有 $F_z=0$，则 $
abla F$ 的 $z$ 分量为零，等值面在该点有竖直切平面，不能局部写成 $z$ 的图，这从几何上解释了条件 $F_z
e0$。

设 $F$ 有连续二阶偏导。求二阶偏导时，$F_x$ 与 $F_z$ 仍通过 $z=\varphi(x,y)$ 依赖 $x$。记 $A=F_x$、$B=F_z$，则 $\varphi_x=-A/B$，且 $A_x=F_{xx}+F_{xz}\varphi_x$、$B_x=F_{zx}+F_{zz}\varphi_x$。于是 $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_{xx}&=-\frac{A_xB-AB_x}{B^2}\\ &=-\frac{F_{xx}F_z^2-2F_{xz}F_xF_z+F_{zz}F_x^2}{F_z^3},\end{aligned}$$ 其中用了 $F_{xz}=F_{zx}$（二阶偏导连续）。右端所有偏导都在 $(x,y,\varphi(x,y))$ 处取值；混合偏导 $\varphi_{xy}$ 可对 $-F_x/F_z$ 关于 $y$ 求导得到。

例：$F=x^2+y^2+z^2-4=0$ 在 $P_0=(1,1,\sqrt2)$ 附近，$F_z=2z=2\sqrt2\ne0$，故确定 $z=\varphi(x,y)$。由 $\varphi_x=-x/z$、$\varphi_y=-y/z$ 得 $\varphi_x(P_0)=\varphi_y(P_0)=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$。再对 $\varphi_x=-x/z$ 关于 $x$ 求导：$$\varphi_{xx}=-\frac{z-xz_x}{z^2}=-\frac{z^2+x^2}{z^3},$$ 在 $P_0$ 处等于 $-\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt2}=-\dfrac{3\sqrt2}{4}$；代入上面的二阶公式也得到同一结果。
en: Let $F(x,y,z)$ have continuous partials in a neighborhood of $P_0=(x_0,y_0,z_0)$, with $F(P_0)=0$ and $F_z(P_0)\ne0$. The implicit function theorem states that there exist a neighborhood $U$ of $(x_0,y_0)$ and a unique continuously differentiable function $z=\varphi(x,y)$, with values near $z_0$, such that $\varphi(x_0,y_0)=z_0$ and $F(x,y,\varphi(x,y))=0$ on $U$. If $F$ has continuous higher-order partials, then $\varphi$ has continuous partials of the corresponding orders.

The condition $F_z(P_0)
e0$ is the key to local solvability. Linearize $F$ at $P_0$: $F(x_0+\Delta x,y_0+\Delta y,z_0+\Delta z)\approx F_x\Delta x+F_y\Delta y+F_z\Delta z$. The coefficient of $\Delta z$ in the linear part is $F_z$; when $F_z
e0$ the linear part determines $\Delta z\approx-\dfrac{F_x\Delta x+F_y\Delta y}{F_z}$, which is the origin of the hypothesis $F_z
e0$. If $F_z=0$, the linearization does not determine $\Delta z$ and the implicit function may fail to exist, may not be unique, or may fail to be differentiable. Counterexample: $F(x,y,z)=z^2-x^2-y^2$ satisfies $F=0$ at the origin but $F_z=0$ there; the equation $z^2=x^2+y^2$ gives two branches $z=\pm\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ near the origin, so it does not define a unique differentiable $z=\varphi(x,y)$ passing through the origin.

Substituting $z=\varphi(x,y)$ into the equation gives the identity $F(x,y,\varphi(x,y))\equiv0$ on $U$. Since $F_z$ is continuous and $F_z(P_0)\ne0$, it remains nonzero in some neighborhood of $P_0$; shrink $U$ if necessary so that division is legitimate there. Holding $y$ fixed and differentiating in $x$, the chain rule gives $$F_x(x,y,\varphi)+F_z(x,y,\varphi)\,\varphi_x=0.$$ Since $F_z\ne0$, we solve $\varphi_x=-\dfrac{F_x}{F_z}$; the same argument in $y$ gives $\varphi_y=-\dfrac{F_y}{F_z}$. All partials are evaluated at $(x,y,\varphi(x,y))$. Thus no explicit formula for $z$ is needed; only the partials of $F$ are required.

Geometric interpretation: $F(x,y,z)=0$ is a level surface with normal $
abla F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$, while the graph $z=\varphi(x,y)$ has normal $(-\varphi_x,-\varphi_y,1)$. The normals are parallel, so $$(-\varphi_x,-\varphi_y,1)= rac{1}{F_z}(F_x,F_y,F_z),$$ hence $\varphi_x=-F_x/F_z$ and $\varphi_y=-F_y/F_z$. If $F_z=0$ while $
abla F(P_0)
e0$, the $z$-component of $
abla F$ vanishes and the level surface has a vertical tangent plane at that point, so it cannot be written locally as a graph over the $xy$-plane; this explains the condition geometrically.

Assume $F$ has continuous second partials. For second partials, $F_x$ and $F_z$ still depend on $x$ through $z=\varphi(x,y)$. Write $A=F_x$, $B=F_z$; then $\varphi_x=-A/B$, with $A_x=F_{xx}+F_{xz}\varphi_x$ and $B_x=F_{zx}+F_{zz}\varphi_x$. Therefore $$\begin{aligned}\varphi_{xx}&=-\frac{A_xB-AB_x}{B^2}\\ &=-\frac{F_{xx}F_z^2-2F_{xz}F_xF_z+F_{zz}F_x^2}{F_z^3},\end{aligned}$$ where $F_{xz}=F_{zx}$ was used (continuous second partials). All partials on the right are evaluated at $(x,y,\varphi(x,y))$; the mixed partial $\varphi_{xy}$ is obtained by differentiating $-F_x/F_z$ in $y$.

Example: $F=x^2+y^2+z^2-4=0$ near $P_0=(1,1,\sqrt2)$. Since $F_z=2z=2\sqrt2\ne0$, the equation defines $z=\varphi(x,y)$. From $\varphi_x=-x/z$ and $\varphi_y=-y/z$ we get $\varphi_x(P_0)=\varphi_y(P_0)=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$. Differentiating $\varphi_x=-x/z$ in $x$ gives $$\varphi_{xx}=-\frac{z-xz_x}{z^2}=-\frac{z^2+x^2}{z^3},$$ which equals $-\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt2}=-\dfrac{3\sqrt2}{4}$ at $P_0$; the second-order formula above gives the same value.

zh: 设 $f$ 在 $(a,b)$ 的某邻域内有直到 $n+1$ 阶连续偏导。固定 $h,k$，令 $g(t)=f(a+th,b+tk)$，$t\in[0,1]$；当 $(h,k)$ 足够小时整条线段落在该邻域内，且 $g$ 有直到 $n+1$ 阶连续导数。对 $g$ 用一元泰勒公式（在 $0$ 处展开、在 $1$ 处取值）：$$g(1)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}\frac{g^{(m)}(0)}{m!}+\frac{g^{(n+1)}(\theta)}{(n+1)!},\qquad \theta\in(0,1).$$ 这样就把多元问题化为一元问题。

由链式法则，$g'(t)=h f_x(a+th,b+tk)+k f_y(a+th,b+tk)=(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)f$。再求导时 $h,k$ 为常数，每作用一次就多一个算子 $(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)$，故归纳得 $$g^{(m)}(t)=(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^m f(a+th,b+tk).$$ 因 $f$ 有连续高阶偏导，混合偏导可交换，展开时可按照二项式定理逐项求偏导。代入 $t=0,1$ 得 $$f(a+h,b+k)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}\frac{1}{m!}(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^m f(a,b)+R_n,$$ $$R_n=\frac{1}{(n+1)!}(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^{n+1}f(a+\theta h,b+\theta k).$$ 这就是带拉格朗日余项的二元泰勒公式。

取 $n=2$。$m=1$ 的项为 $hf_x+kf_y$；$m=2$ 时 $(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^2=h^2\partial_{xx}+2hk\partial_{xy}+k^2\partial_{yy}$，故 $$\begin{aligned}f(a+h,b+k)&=f(a,b)+hf_x+kf_y\\ &\quad+\frac{1}{2}\left(h^2f_{xx}+2hkf_{xy}+k^2f_{yy}\right)+R_2,\end{aligned}$$ 所有偏导均在 $(a,b)$ 取值。交叉项系数 $2hk$ 来自 $hk$ 与 $kh$ 两项合并；若二阶混合偏导连续，则 $f_{xy}=f_{yx}$，二次项可写成 $\dfrac12\mathbf h^TH(a,b)\mathbf h$，其中 $\mathbf h=(h,k)^T$，$H=\begin{pmatrix}f_{xx}&f_{xy}\\f_{xy}&f_{yy}\end{pmatrix}$ 为 Hessian 矩阵。

若只假设 $f$ 在 $(a,b)$ 附近有直到 $n$ 阶连续偏导，则余项可弱化为佩亚诺形式 $R_n=o(\rho^n)$，其中 $\rho=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}\to0$。证明可用一元泰勒公式的积分余项：对 $g(t)$ 有 $$g(1)-\sum_{m=0}^{n}\frac{g^{(m)}(0)}{m!}=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\left[g^{(n)}(t)-g^{(n)}(0)\right]dt.$$ 而 $g^{(n)}(t)$ 是形如 $h^\alpha k^\beta f_{(\alpha,\beta)}(a+th,b+tk)$（$|\alpha|+|\beta|=n$）的项之和；各 $n$ 阶偏导在紧邻域上一致连续，故 $|g^{(n)}(t)-g^{(n)}(0)|\le\rho^n\varepsilon(h,k)$，其中 $\varepsilon(h,k)\to0$。积分后即得 $R_n=o(\rho^n)$。$n=1$ 的展开 $f(a+h,b+k)=f(a,b)+f_xh+f_yk+o(\rho)$ 表明全微分是函数增量的线性主部。注意佩亚诺余项只给出误差阶，不能用于具体数值误差估计；后者需要拉格朗日余项或高阶导数的一致界。

在驻点 $\nabla f(a,b)=\boldsymbol0$ 处一次项消失，于是 $$\Delta f=f(a+h,b+k)-f(a,b)=\frac12\mathbf h^TH(a,b)\mathbf h+o(\rho^2).$$ 若 $H$ 正定，设最小特征值 $\lambda_1>0$，则 $\mathbf h^TH\mathbf h\ge\lambda_1\rho^2$，二次项压过余项，故 $f$ 在 $(a,b)$ 取严格极小；$H$ 负定时取严格极大；$H$ 不定时，沿正、负特征方向 $\Delta f$ 分别取正、负，故为鞍点。若 $H$ 半定（包括奇异），二阶判别法失效，需考察更高阶项。

例：$f(x,y)=e^x\cos y$ 在 $(0,0)$ 处。$f(0,0)=1$，$f_x=e^x\cos y$、$f_y=-e^x\sin y$，故 $f_x(0,0)=1$、$f_y(0,0)=0$；$f_{xx}=e^x\cos y$、$f_{xy}=-e^x\sin y$、$f_{yy}=-e^x\cos y$，在原点分别为 $1,0,-1$。于是 $$f(x,y)=1+x+\frac12(x^2-y^2)+o(x^2+y^2).$$ 二次型 $x^2-y^2$ 不定，但 $f_x(0,0)=1\ne0$，原点不是驻点，因此不能据此说原点是鞍点；这正说明二阶判别法只在驻点处使用。
en: Let $f$ have continuous partials up to order $n+1$ in a neighborhood of $(a,b)$. Fix $h,k$ and set $g(t)=f(a+th,b+tk)$ for $t\in[0,1]$; for $(h,k)$ small enough the whole segment lies in that neighborhood and $g$ has continuous derivatives up to order $n+1$. Apply the one-variable Taylor formula to $g$ (expanded at $0$ and evaluated at $1$): $$g(1)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}\frac{g^{(m)}(0)}{m!}+\frac{g^{(n+1)}(\theta)}{(n+1)!},\qquad \theta\in(0,1).$$ This reduces the multivariable problem to a one-variable one.

By the chain rule, $g'(t)=h f_x(a+th,b+tk)+k f_y(a+th,b+tk)=(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)f$. Since $h,k$ are constants, each differentiation adds another operator $(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)$; induction gives $$g^{(m)}(t)=(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^m f(a+th,b+tk).$$ Because $f$ has continuous higher partials, mixed partials commute, so the operator can be expanded by the binomial theorem and differentiated term by term. Substituting $t=0,1$ yields $$f(a+h,b+k)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}\frac{1}{m!}(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^m f(a,b)+R_n,$$ $$R_n=\frac{1}{(n+1)!}(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^{n+1}f(a+\theta h,b+\theta k).$$ This is Taylor's formula in two variables with the Lagrange remainder.

Take $n=2$. The $m=1$ term is $hf_x+kf_y$; for $m=2$, $(h\partial_x+k\partial_y)^2=h^2\partial_{xx}+2hk\partial_{xy}+k^2\partial_{yy}$, hence $$\begin{aligned}f(a+h,b+k)&=f(a,b)+hf_x+kf_y\\ &\quad+\frac{1}{2}\left(h^2f_{xx}+2hkf_{xy}+k^2f_{yy}\right)+R_2,\end{aligned}$$ with all partials evaluated at $(a,b)$. The factor $2hk$ comes from combining the $hk$ and $kh$ terms; if the mixed second partials are continuous, $f_{xy}=f_{yx}$ and the quadratic part becomes $\dfrac12\mathbf h^TH(a,b)\mathbf h$, where $\mathbf h=(h,k)^T$ and $H=\begin{pmatrix}f_{xx}&f_{xy}\\f_{xy}&f_{yy}\end{pmatrix}$ is the Hessian.

If $f$ is only assumed to have continuous partials up to order $n$ near $(a,b)$, the remainder weakens to the Peano form $R_n=o(\rho^n)$, where $\rho=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}\to0$. The proof uses the integral remainder for $g$: $$g(1)-\sum_{m=0}^{n}\frac{g^{(m)}(0)}{m!}=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\left[g^{(n)}(t)-g^{(n)}(0)\right]dt.$$ Now $g^{(n)}(t)$ is a sum of terms $h^\alpha k^\beta f_{(\alpha,\beta)}(a+th,b+tk)$ with $|\alpha|+|\beta|=n$; the $n$-th partials are uniformly continuous on a compact neighborhood, so $|g^{(n)}(t)-g^{(n)}(0)|\le\rho^n\varepsilon(h,k)$ with $\varepsilon(h,k)\to0$. Integrating gives $R_n=o(\rho^n)$. For $n=1$, $f(a+h,b+k)=f(a,b)+f_xh+f_yk+o(\rho)$ says that the total differential is the linear principal part of the increment. The Peano remainder only gives the order of the error, not a numerical bound; the latter requires the Lagrange remainder or a uniform bound on higher derivatives.

At a stationary point $\nabla f(a,b)=\boldsymbol0$ the linear term vanishes, so $$\Delta f=f(a+h,b+k)-f(a,b)=\frac12\mathbf h^TH(a,b)\mathbf h+o(\rho^2).$$ If $H$ is positive definite with smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_1>0$, then $\mathbf h^TH\mathbf h\ge\lambda_1\rho^2$, the quadratic term dominates the remainder, and $f$ has a strict local minimum at $(a,b)$; negative definiteness gives a strict maximum; if $H$ is indefinite, $\Delta f$ is positive along the positive eigenvector and negative along the negative one, so $(a,b)$ is a saddle. If $H$ is semidefinite (including singular), the second-order test is inconclusive and higher-order terms must be examined.

Example: $f(x,y)=e^x\cos y$ at $(0,0)$. Here $f(0,0)=1$, $f_x=e^x\cos y$, $f_y=-e^x\sin y$, so $f_x(0,0)=1$ and $f_y(0,0)=0$; $f_{xx}=e^x\cos y$, $f_{xy}=-e^x\sin y$, $f_{yy}=-e^x\cos y$, which equal $1,0,-1$ at the origin. Hence $$f(x,y)=1+x+\frac12(x^2-y^2)+o(x^2+y^2).$$ The quadratic form $x^2-y^2$ is indefinite, but $f_x(0,0)=1\ne0$, so the origin is not a stationary point and one cannot conclude that it is a saddle; this illustrates that the second-order test applies only at stationary points.
